name: Arjuna
summary: The addressee of BhG 4–6 (so called by the vocatives Pārtha, Kaunteya, Bhārata, Parantapa, Mahābāho, Dhanañjaya, Pāṇḍava, Kurusattama, Kurunandana). He receives the ancient yoga as the Lord's devotee and friend (4.3); he asks how the Lord could have taught Vivasvat (4.4), which is better, renunciation or yoga (5.1), how the restless mind can be steadied (6.33–34), and what becomes of one who falls from yoga (6.37–39).

name: Ikṣvāku
summary: Bhagavad Gītā 4.1: received the yoga from Manu; after him the royal sages knew it through succession until it was lost over time (4.2).

name: Kṛṣṇa
summary: In BhG 4–6 the speaker (śrī bhagavān), addressed as Kṛṣṇa (5.1, 6.34, 6.37, 6.39) and Madhusūdana (6.33). He says he first taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvat (4.1), knows all his many births (4.5), and, unborn and lord of beings, comes into being by his own māyā age after age to establish dharma (4.6–8); he is enjoyer of sacrifices, great lord of all worlds and friend of all beings (5.29), the object of the meditator's thought (6.14), and the one whose faithful worshipper is the most yoked yogin (6.47).

name: Manu (Vaivasvata)
summary: Bhagavad Gītā 4.1: Vivasvat told the yoga to Manu, and Manu told it to Ikṣvāku. The text says only 'Manu'; commentators identify him as Vivasvat's son.

name: Vivasvat
summary: Named in Bhagavad Gītā 4.1 as the first to receive the imperishable yoga from Kṛṣṇa, who told it to Manu; Arjuna objects that Vivasvat's birth was earlier than Kṛṣṇa's (4.4). The text does not further identify him (tradition: the Sun).
